# PitCrew reference

Every command, setting, file, environment variable, exit code and hook of PitCrew. For tasks, see
the [how-to guides](how-to.md); for what it cannot do, see the [limitations](limitations.md).

## Commands

`pitcrew` runs in the session's Bash tool, where PitCrew puts it on the `PATH`; the skills run it
for you. Run with no argument or with an unknown group, it prints a usage text that names both
groups and exits 2. If `pitcrew` is not found, run `python
"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/pitcrew.py"` with the same arguments. The table is read from the
plugin's own command parser.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `pitcrew context-watch` | warnings before auto-compaction, snapshots at each compaction |
| `pitcrew context-watch config` | show or change context-watch's settings |
| `pitcrew context-watch status` | show the settings, the snapshot folder and the settings file |
| `pitcrew cache-watch` | keep an idle session's one-hour prompt cache alive |
| `pitcrew cache-watch on` | watch one session |
| `pitcrew cache-watch off` | stop watching one session |
| `pitcrew cache-watch status` | list the watched sessions |
| `pitcrew cache-watch config` | show or change the defaults for every session |

### cache-watch commands

- `pitcrew cache-watch on --session ID --data-dir DIR [--lead MIN] [--max N]` watches one session;
  `DIR` is the plugin's data directory, where the session's state lives. It exits 3 and prints `not
  started` with the reason when it finds no transcript for the session, no one-hour cache entry yet,
  or five-minute cache entries. cache-watch holds only the one-hour prompt cache; when the main
  thread switches to five-minute entries while watching, it stops itself, and `status` shows the
  session as `off (five-minute cache)`. After the session line, `on` prints two lines on what a wake
  costs: the context size, and that a rewrite of the context after the cache expired costs at least
  20 times a wake's cache read. See [limitations](limitations.md#cache-watch).
- `pitcrew cache-watch off --session ID --data-dir DIR` stops watching a session.
- `pitcrew cache-watch status --data-dir DIR` lists every watched session: on or off and why
  (`operator`, `five-minute cache`, `no reply after N wakes`, `compacted`, `cache expired before the
  wake`), the wakes so far, the cache expiry, and the next wake. It removes the state of sessions
  whose transcript has not changed for 24 hours.
- `pitcrew cache-watch config [--lead MIN] [--max N]` shows or changes the defaults: `lead` is 5
  minutes (1 to 30), and `max` is 5 wakes (1 to 20). It prints `defaults: lead 5 min · max 5 wakes
  without a reply`, and writes `<state>/cache-watch.json` only when an option is given. `--lead` and
  `--max` on `on` apply to that session only. A wake comes `lead` minutes before the cache expires,
  and no later than 52.5 minutes after the last request.

The data directory is the plugin's `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}`; it holds the state of each watched
session. The defaults are not there: they are in `<state>/cache-watch.json`. The skill
`/pitcrew:cache-watch` fills in the session ID and the data directory.

### context-watch commands

- `pitcrew context-watch status [--project DIR]` prints the settings, the project's snapshot folder
  with its number of snapshots, and PitCrew's settings file. When the settings were read from
  PaceLine's file, a last line says `settings read from <path> (from PaceLine)`. `DIR` defaults to
  the current directory.
- `pitcrew context-watch config [--on|--off] [--line on|off] [--levels 85,95] [--days N]` shows or
  changes the settings. `--off` turns off the line, the warnings, and the snapshots. `--line on`
  adds the line to every prompt; `--line off` hides it, which is the default. Levels are ascending
  whole percents from 50 to 99. Snapshots are kept 1 to 90 days. It prints `context-watch on · line
  off · warn at 85%, 95% of the auto-compact point · snapshots kept 14 days` with the current
  values, and writes the settings only when an option is given. Changes apply from the next prompt.

Defaults: on, line off, warnings at 85% and 95%, snapshots kept 14 days.

## Settings

context-watch has four settings and cache-watch two defaults. The table is read from the plugin's
own constants. A stored value outside its range reads as the default, each setting on its own. The
levels of context-watch must rise: each level is above the one before it, otherwise the list reads
as the default.

| Watcher | Key | Default | Range |
|---|---|---|---|
| context-watch | `on` | `true` | on or off |
| context-watch | `line` | `false` | on or off |
| context-watch | `levels` | `[85, 95]` | 50–99 |
| context-watch | `snapshot_days` | `14` | 1–90 |
| cache-watch | `lead_minutes` | `5` | 1–30 |
| cache-watch | `max_wakes` | `5` | 1–20 |

PitCrew's settings files are `context-watch.json` and `cache-watch.json` in its state directory.
They are read in this order, for each file on its own:

1. The file in PitCrew's state directory, when it exists. It is then the only source; a field it
   lacks or holds out of range reads as the default.
2. Else the file of the same name in PaceLine's state directory, which PaceLine 0.6.0 and earlier
   wrote.
3. Else the defaults.

A `config` command always writes the whole settings object to PitCrew's state directory. PaceLine's
files are never written, moved or deleted. `pitcrew context-watch status` names the file the
settings were read from.

## Skills

Each skill runs the matching command for you:

- `/pitcrew:context-watch status|config`
- `/pitcrew:cache-watch on|off|status|config`

## Files and folders

`<state>` is PitCrew's state directory: `$PITCREW_STATE_DIR` when set, else
`<config>/state/pitcrew`. `<config>` is `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, else `~/.claude`. `<legacy>` is
PaceLine's: `$PACELINE_STATE_DIR`, else `<config>/state/paceline`.

| Path | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `<state>/context-watch.json` | context-watch settings: `on`, `line`, `levels`, `snapshot_days`. PitCrew writes it when a `config` command changes a value. |
| `<state>/cache-watch.json` | The defaults of cache-watch, `lead_minutes` and `max_wakes`. A value outside its range reads as the default. |
| `<legacy>/context-watch.json` | PaceLine's copy of the settings. Read only while `<state>/context-watch.json` does not exist; never written, moved or deleted. |
| `<legacy>/cache-watch.json` | PaceLine's copy of the defaults, read under the same rule. |
| `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}/cache-watch/<session id>.json` | cache-watch state of one session. Not carried over from PaceLine's data directory. |
| `<project>/.claude/pitcrew/<session id>.md` | context-watch snapshots. The folder has its own `.gitignore` (`*`), so git ignores it. Snapshots older than the snapshot days are removed at session start. |
| `<project>/.claude/paceline/*.md` | Snapshots PaceLine wrote. PitCrew removes those older than the snapshot days at session start and touches nothing else in the folder. |
| `<config>/projects/<project>/<session id>.jsonl` | The session transcript, a private file of Claude Code. cache-watch reads it for the main thread's cache writes; it never writes it. |

## Environment variables

| Variable | What it does |
|---|---|
| `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` | Claude Code's configuration directory. PitCrew's state directory and PaceLine's are under it, and cache-watch looks for transcripts in its `projects` folder. Unset or empty: `~/.claude`. |
| `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA` | The plugin's data directory, set by Claude Code for hooks. cache-watch keeps each watched session's state there. The Bash tool does not have it, so the skill passes `--data-dir`. |
| `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` | The project whose old snapshots are removed at session start. When it is not set, the `cwd` of the hook's input is used. |
| `HOME` | Where the module finds the home directory to compute `<config>` when `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is not set and `USERPROFILE` is not set. |
| `PACELINE_STATE_DIR` | PaceLine's state directory, which PitCrew reads settings from while it has none of its own. Unset or empty: `<config>/state/paceline`. |
| `PITCREW_STATE_DIR` | PitCrew's state directory. Unset or empty: `<config>/state/pitcrew`. |
| `USERPROFILE` | Where the module finds the home directory to compute `<config>` when `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is not set; `HOME` is the fallback. |

The module reads the variables from the environment Claude Code starts in. The table is checked
against the variables PitCrew's code reads.

## Exit codes

- `0`: success.
- `1`: a refused value, with the message on stderr as `pitcrew context-watch: ...` or `pitcrew
  cache-watch: ...`, for example `levels must be ascending whole percents 50-99, e.g. 85,95`, `days
  must be 1-90`, `lead must be 1-30 minutes` or `max must be 1-20`. A refused value changes nothing.
- `2`: an invalid command line, or `pitcrew` with no group or an unknown one.
- `3`: `cache-watch on` uses 3 for `not started`.

## Hooks

| Hook | When | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Module: `UserPromptSubmit`, `PostToolBatch`, `session.compact`, `SessionStart` after a compaction | Every prompt, tool batch, and compaction | context-watch. Does nothing while context-watch is off, and never vetoes a compaction. |
| `Stop`: `cache_watch.py hook stop` | After every turn | Waits for the next wake of a watched session; returns at once for any other session. When the cache expired before the wake, turns the session off with the reason `cache expired before the wake`. |
| `UserPromptSubmit`: `cache_watch.py hook prompt` | Every prompt | Resets the wake count of a watched session. After a cache that expired before its wake, adds a one-time notice for the agent to pass on. |
| `PreCompact`, `SessionStart` (`compact`): `cache_watch.py hook compact` | Before and after a compaction, manual or automatic | Turns a watched session off with the reason `compacted`, which also ends its waiting `Stop` hook. |
| `SessionEnd`: `cache_watch.py hook session-end` | Session end | Removes the session's cache-watch state. |
| `SessionStart`: `context_watch.py hook session-start` | Session start | Removes old snapshots while context-watch is on. |

The command hooks run `python3` when it works, else `python`. While a watcher is off, its command
hooks still start one Python process per matching event. A cache-watch wake starts its prompt with
`pitcrew cache-watch woke this session`; PaceLine recognises a wake by `cache-watch woke this
session`, so a wake does not clear PaceLine's away marker.

## Requirements

- Claude Code 2.1.287 or later.
- Python 3.9 or later on `PATH` as `python3` or `python`, in the environment Claude Code starts in.
  PitCrew uses the standard library only.
- cache-watch needs an interactive session whose main thread writes one-hour cache entries. See
  [Limitations](limitations.md#cache-watch).
